_comment: D-31 decision table for the re-approach fork (cap-menu option 5 / D-2 exhaustion-fork branch 4). Machine-checked by tools/check-reapproach-invariants.py. Eligibility is MECHANICALLY DERIVED from each case's open_blockers: ELIGIBLE iff every blocker is contract-mechanics class AND none cites a requirement id. A blocker citing only task or contract ids is contract-mechanics by construction; a blocker citing an R-id means the requirement itself is in dispute, which re-authoring contracts cannot answer. Bounded to at most once per objective: already_used_this_objective forces INELIGIBLE regardless of how clean the blockers are. An IMPOSSIBLE-COMMAND verifier verdict (policy/acceptance-contract.md) always routes to re-approach independent of blocker composition.

cases.why: a first-time selection with only contract-mechanics blockers that cite no requirement id is the healthy path: re-authoring contracts can answer this
the once-per-objective bound overrides even a perfectly clean blocker set — a second re-approach on the same objective is never eligible
an open blocker that is not contract-mechanics class is a substantive plan or requirements defect, not a contract-authoring problem
a finding that cites a requirement id disputes the requirement itself; re-authoring the acceptance contracts cannot answer that dispute
blockers citing only task or contract ids are contract-mechanics by construction, so the predicate must not reject them
an IMPOSSIBLE-COMMAND verdict is a CONTRACT defect (policy/acceptance-contract.md) and always routes to re-approach, never to a work-defect retry, independent of blocker composition
